newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's teachers to strike against austerity.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's teachers to strike against austerity.

text.p: Ecuador President Abdala Bucaram's five-month-old administration will face its first labor protest Wednesday when teachers go on strike against economic austerity policies.
The National Teachers Union (UNE) said Tuesday it hopes most of its 127,000 members will back the protest, which would cripple public schools attended by some 2.3 million students.

"The aim of the protest is to oppose the set of economic and wage measures announced by the president, as well as to reject regulations which allow (the government) to replace school authorities," UNE president Stalin Vargas told Reuters.
He said the Education Ministry also threatened to fire teachers who back the strike.
Bucaram warned 1997 would be a tough year for the population after the government recently announced new taxes and scrapped subsidies for gas, electricity and gasoline.
The savings will help finance a fiscal deficit equal to about four percent of Gross Domestic Product and will set the framework for a currency convertibility plan.
Ecuador's minimum monthly wage was also frozen at 95,000 sucres ($25.99). Teachers with 10 years seniority earn 463,000 sucres (126.6 dollars).
